tagline: AI · dev tools · tech — a two-minute read

lead.headline: Google answers Fable with Gemini 4 Carbon, now #1 on CursorBench, plus a /swarm mode for agent teams
lead.summary: A day after Anthropic's Fable 5.2, Google opened up Gemini 4 Carbon, its model for long, multi-step coding, debugging and research. Google says it ranks first on CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity's WANDR and Zapier's AutomationBench at more than 2x lower cost per task than the next-best outside model. It costs $2/$10 per million tokens until 30 November, then $4/$20. Google Antigravity also previews /swarm, which turns one prompt into a team of agents, with Carbon taking the design, coordination and audit roles.

number_of_day.label: Anthropic's run-rate revenue at the end of October, up $10B in a single month, per its amended IPO filing.

news.headline: DeepMind's AlphaProof Code proves Signal's core crypto secure, down to the compiled machine code
news.summary: Humans and AI wrote the specs; Carbon-powered prover agents then produced about 6.5 million lines of Lean proof in four weeks, covering the PQXDH handshake and Triple Ratchet. Agents flagged about 1% for human review. When two old, fixed bugs were put back in, the system proved that version insecure.

news.headline: Anthropic sets its IPO at $70–78 a share, up to a $1.4T valuation, trading as ANT
news.summary: 825 million shares, pricing on 18 November and trading from the 19th, according to CNBC's sources, with about 20% earmarked for retail. AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC will buy $26B more in a private placement at the IPO price.

news.headline: Claude joins your Google Meet calls and builds things while you talk
news.summary: Claude Meetings, in beta for Team and Enterprise, adds Claude as a visible participant that drafts plans and timelines and answers questions in chat during the call. Anthropic also launched Claude Whiteboards, Claude Sheets and Claude Data.

news.headline: Copenhagen's Sumary raises a $25M seed to automate accounting firms' month-end closes
news.summary: Singular led the round, and the angels include Linear's Tuomas Artman. Sumary says firms spend 50% less time on monthly closes and 75% less on VAT returns after three months, and that it already works with most of the Nordics' 20 largest accounting firms.

x_posts.name: Cursor
x_posts.text: Your agents can now coordinate with your teammates’ agents. Projects has been rebuilt for multiplayer: every teammate and their agents can now work together in one unified workspace.
x_posts.why: Coding agents go multiplayer: worth a look if your team already runs agents side by side.

x_posts.name: Guillermo Rauch
x_posts.text: Rust is a superb language and ecosystem, especially given it was invented pre agentic coding. With agents, new languages will blossom, even purpose-built ones for specific usecases, and discretionary C or even LLVM IR, assembly… AI is fluid. No more one-size-fits-all.
x_posts.why: A bet that agents will weaken the pull toward one default language.

x_posts.why: Unreal Engine 5.9's MegaJam Preview lets you work with AI coding agents right in the editor, and opencode is one of them.

x_posts.name: Hamel Husain
x_posts.text: The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is currently made up of 9 benchmarks with arbitrary weights. I wanted to know how these weights varied over time. They vary quite a bit!
x_posts.why: Useful for this week of new models: a reminder to look inside the leaderboard number before trusting it.

writers_corner.title: Fable 5.2 and Jagged AGI
writers_corner.take: Mollick puts Fable 5.2 to work as a filmmaker, hardware hacker, founder, scholar and world-builder, and calls it 'almost AGI'. What's still missing is noticing on its own when its work is joyless, bloated or tangled in red tape.
writers_corner.quote: If building a bureaucracy disqualified you from general intelligence, a lot of us would be in trouble.
